{{short description|British statistician (born 1930)}}
'''E. Joyce Snell''' (born 1930){{r|born}} is a British [[statistician]] who taught in the mathematics department at [[Imperial College London]].
She is known for her work on [[Errors and residuals|residuals]] and [[Ordinal data|ordered categorical data]], and for her books on statistics.

==Books==
Snell is the author or editor of:
*''Analysis of Binary Data'' (with [[David Cox (statistician)|David R. Cox]], 1969; 2nd ed., Chapman & Hall/CRC, 1989){{r|ab}}
*''Applied Statistics: Principles and Examples'' (with [[David Cox (statistician)|David R. Cox]], Chapman & Hall/CRC, 1981){{r|pe}}
*''Applied Statistics: A Handbook of GENSTAT Analyses'' (with H. R. Simpson, 1982){{r|gen}}
*''Applied Statistics: A Handbook of BMDP Analyses'' (Chapman & Hall/CRC, 1987){{r|bm}}
*''Statistical Theory and Modelling: in Honour of Sir David Cox, FRS'' (edited with [[David Hinkley]] and [[Nancy Reid]], Chapman & Hall/CRC, 1991){{r|stm}}

==Recognition==
Snell was given the {{ill|Chambers Medal|pt|Medalha Chambers}} of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] in 1986 "for her outstanding service to the Society", and in particular for her work organizing the 150th anniversary celebration for the society.{{r|chambers}}
